files.description: The 30 lines of Psych-101 prompts_training.jsonl whose experiment == 'xiong2023neural/exp1.csv' (one line per participant, all 6 games). The datasets-server /filter endpoint was failing (HF auth error), so the full jsonl was streamed at the pinned revision and filtered on the fly (grep -F 'xiong2023neural/exp1.csv'). Only the matching lines were stored.
files.upstream_sha_check: streamed sha256 equals the HF x-linked-etag (LFS oid)

files.description: Raw per-trial data: task, trial, choice (0/1), reward, RT, slot1_value, slot2_value (true expected points), hazard_rate, block_length, participant. 155,400 rows, 33 participants.
files.license: NONE DECLARED (the dataset card has no license field). Treat as all rights reserved: use it for research analysis and do not redistribute. Cite the paper below.

paper.citation: Xiong, H.-D., Ji-An, L., Mattar, M. G., & Wilson, R. C. (2023). Neural network modeling reveals diverse human exploration behaviors via state space analysis. Conference on Cognitive Computational Neuroscience (CCN 2023), pp. 1335-1337.

psych101_citation: Binz, M., et al. (2025). A foundation model to predict and capture human cognition. Nature (Centaur / Psych-101).

cross_check.psych101_vs_raw: For all 30 Psych-101 participants (ids = raw participant ids), all 6 games (180) match the raw choices and rewards trial-for-trial.
cross_check.paper_vs_data: The paper reports 29 participants, 3 x 1500-trial blocks and a 300-trial practice. The data have 33 raw / 30 Psych-101 participants. The 100-trial games appear to be the practice (3 x 100 = 300).
cross_check.reward_noise: reward == chosen machine's current true value on every trial (155,400/155,400 rows). The task is noise-free; the points change only at change points (hazard h).
